signature.name: Grand Place
signature.detail: Brussels' central square is a UNESCO-listed ensemble of gilded guildhalls and the ornate Town Hall, and it is the city's undisputed icon. Come early in the morning for uncrowded photos, and return after dark when the buildings are floodlit.

signature.name: Atomium
signature.detail: The futuristic 1958 World's Fair structure is Brussels' most recognizable modern landmark, with panoramic views from its spheres. Take metro line 6 to Heysel and book tickets online to skip the queue.

signature.name: Manneken Pis
signature.detail: This tiny bronze statue of a urinating boy is a beloved symbol of Brussels' irreverent humor. It is a quick stop near Grand Place, so combine it with a walk through the nearby streets.

signature.name: Royal Palace of Brussels
signature.detail: The official palace of the Belgian monarchy faces Brussels Park and is open to visitors in summer. Check opening dates before you go, as it is only accessible for part of the year.

signature.name: St Michael and St Gudula Cathedral
signature.detail: This Gothic cathedral is a majestic landmark with stunning stained glass and a royal history. Entry is free, and it is a short walk uphill from Grand Place.

signature.name: Parc du Cinquantenaire
signature.detail: The park's triumphal arch and surrounding museums make it a grand, green escape from the city center. Visit on a sunny day and combine it with the nearby Royal Museum of the Armed Forces.
